column7: Camponotus consobrinus (Hymenoptera: Formicidae); adult workers, minor ("foragers") and major ("soldiers") castes. Castes separated by size (head width 1.79 ± 0.11 vs 3.06 ± 0.30 mm; n = 20 each, non-overlapping). ID to species level using McArthur (2007)

column4: Origin: wild-collected (with locality and date), laboratory colony (founding stock, source, date of establishment), or commercial supplier (named). For captive stock: generations in captivity, rearing conditions, and selection or inbreeding history.
column7: Wild-collected at civil twilight from outbound trails of one monogyne colony throughout 19/12/25 - 22/02/26 (DD/MM/YY) at a field site in Ku-ring-gai. Not captive-reared.

column4: Total individuals collected or used and number contributing to analysis, with attrition accounted for. Justification of sample size (a priori power, pilot data, or stated convention). For bulk-sampling or mass-rearing work, report order-of-magnitude counts or ranges, and the unit of replication (colony, cycle, trap-day, batch), rather than individual totals.
column7: Pilot: 180 (15 per caste × 6 temperatures). Main: 192 (32 per caste × treatment); 171 analysed (16 corrupted video or injured; 5 did not groom). Power analysis (pwr) pwr.f2.test(u=3, v=NULL, f2=0.35, sig.level = 0.05, power = 0.8)

column4: Capture method; transport duration, conditions, and mortality. Routine handling and restraint. Marking or tagging method, tag mass where relevant, retention checks. Where individual handling is not practicable (pitfall, Malaise, light, or sticky trapping and similar), report sampling effort (trap-days, trap-nights, deployment volume), trap design and check routine, and measures taken to reduce by-catch, retention time, and trapped-animal suffering.
column7: Hand-collected by letting ants walk onto a sheet of paper or stick and off into the container. Restrained under a sponge for c. 5 s during treatment (no-touch controls likewise). Paint dot on mesosoma (Citadel) after testing to prevent retesting.

column4: Anaesthetic or immobilisation agent or method; induction and recovery times; justification. Whether post-procedure analgesia was used, agent and dose, or explicit justification for omission. For surgical/invasive procedures: procedure, instruments, sterility, duration, recovery.
column7: No anaesthesia or surgery. Single 5 s contact of a 55°C chisel-tip probe (Hakko FX-888D) with the first funicular segment of one antenna. No analgesia, as it would suppress the responses under study.

column4: Measures to prevent escape (particularly for non-native taxa) and procedures for disposal of waste and contaminated material.
column7: Native species; held with nestmates and returned to colony. Arena ethanol-wiped between trials. Waste products were stored and then disposed in the appropriate secure biohazard bins

IUCN, national, or regional conservation status of focal taxa. Country, state, and any translocation between jurisdictions, including distance from point of collection where relevant.
column7: No ethics review required; insects not covered by animal-research legislation in New South Wales, Australia. No collection permit required. Not of conservation concern. No translocation.

column4: Predefined criteria for terminating procedures or experiments early in response to welfare concerns, and any instances triggered. For field work: anticipated and observed non-target impacts, with mitigation.
column7: Predefined endpoint was following the ten minute assay or if an ant was obviously greviously injured in such a way that normal walking gait was impared. Injured ants excluded from analysis. Laboratory study; no non-target impacts.

column4: Brief statement summarising welfare considerations and how the three Rs (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) informed study design.
column7: Replacement: whole-animal behaviour, no alternative; literature search confirmed no prior assay in this species. Reduction: a priori power analysis; videos archived for re-use. Refinement: pilot-calibrated temperature; single brief contact on one segment; ≤48 h holding with nestmates; return to nest.

column4: Composition and source of diet or bait; preparation; feeding frequency and access; provision of water or moisture; any pre- or post-experimental fasting with justification.
column7: Water and 10% sugar solution ad libitum during holding (≤48 h); no fasting. Cotton swaps soaked in each solution were presented in a shallow dish to avoid accidental drowning, and were replaced daily to minimise disease. No protein were provided for adult ants.

column4: Enclosure materials, dimensions, substrate, and structural complexity. Stocking density and grouping. Temperature, humidity, ventilation, photoperiod and lighting, and water parameters for aquatic species. Enclosure cleaning frequency and protocol.
column7: Groups of nestmates in a container in a dark cupboard to approximate nest conditions. Container was 45 cm × 30 cm × 20 cm (W × D × H), with large holes drilled in the top for ventilation. Substrate was a coco peat and wood chip mix filled to approximately 3 cm. Temperature were a stable 21°C and humidity was unknown, largely owing to variable humidity fluctuations from exposed liquids in a contained cupboard environment. Arena size was 10 × 10 × 5 glass container rimmed with fluon, and was dimly lit by a Godox ML60 fitted with a red filter.

column4: Duration and conditions of any acclimation period before experimental procedures.
column7: 5 min in the test arena before treatment. No more than 48 hours between collection and testing.

column4: Habitat type, location, abiotic conditions, and seasonality. Trap design, placement, deployment duration, checking frequency, and measures to limit injury, predation, exposure, or desiccation.
column7: Collected from the outbound foraging trail of one colony at civil twilight. Urban/forest boundary habitat during warm summer season. No traps.

column4: Methods and criteria for assessing physical condition (responsiveness, posture, integument, autotomy). Any screening for disease or parasites and quarantine procedures. Frequency of welfare checks.
column7: Pilot: antennal use scored 0 / 0.5 / 1 as an injury proxy; ants monitored for 24 h. Main: injuries (missing limbs, limping) identified from video.

column4: Number and timing of injuries and unexpected deaths, suspected causes, and any interventions or protocol adjustments. For colony or industrial-scale work where individual death counts are not meaningful (because of scale, cannibalism, or routine attrition), report the disease-screening and prevention regime, density and condition monitoring, and any conditions under which cohort losses triggered intervention or protocol change.
column7: Pilot: mean antennal use < 1 from 50°C in foragers and 60°C in soldiers (Supp. Mat. 1); 24 hr scores recorded for all ants. Main: seven files corrputed and nine ants injured. There were no deaths in held ants.

column4: Method of killing (euthanasia, sacrifice, or slaughter as contextually appropriate) and justification; release protocols for field-collected animals; continued holding, rehoming, or transfer arrangements; voucher specimen deposition. For mass-rearing work, use the welfare-community terminology for the context (slaughter method for farmed insects). For studies considering release, note the reasoning behind the choice between release, continued holding, rehoming, and slaughter, including disease-spread risk to wild conspecifics and any maladaptation incurred during captivity.
column7: None killed as injuries were only noticed in slowed down videos given the speed and variablitly of ants following treatment application; all ants returned to their nest of origin within 48 h of collection. Given the sterile condition ants were held in, and their short retention time, we decided there was low risk of contaminating the nest with released animals. Pilot: ants with impared antennae were released to the colony after 24 hours of observation, to which they apparently returned to normal behaviour. In future we will consider immediate slaugther of these impared animals given the uncertainty surrounding long-term antennal damage.

column7: Held with nestmates in darkness; holding limited to ≤48 h. Tested singly and left undisturbed during the 10 min recording.

column4: Taxon-appropriate behavioural and physiological indicators of stress, pain, or distress monitored, and how interpreted. Where capacity for affective experience is uncertain, the precautionary measures adopted.
column7: Site-directed grooming (frequency, duration, time course) was the outcome measure, interpreted as a potential pain-like indicator; antennal posture and use (pilot) as injury indicators. Precaution: limiting temperature, single exposure, brief holding.
